findings.summary: request.data.dict() crashes for JSON POST because request.data returns a plain dict from json.loads(), not a QueryDict with a .dict() method
findings.failure_scenario: A JSON POST request (Content-Type: application/json) triggers the dev middleware to call request_as_dict(). At line 140, request.data.dict() raises AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'dict', crashing the request-logging path.

findings.summary: json.JSONDecodeError from request.data.get() bypasses the UnreadablePostError handler in the CSRF middleware, causing a 500 error instead of a 403
findings.failure_scenario: A POST request with Content-Type: application/json and an invalid JSON body reaches a CSRF-protected view. request.data.get('_csrftoken', '') at line 367 triggers _load_data_and_files(), which calls json.loads(self.body) and raises json.JSONDecodeError on malformed JSON. The except UnreadablePostError at line 368 does not catch json.JSONDecodeError, so the exception propagates to _get_csrf_response which only catches RejectRequest, resulting in an unhandled 500 error instead of the expected 403 response.

findings.summary: Stale comment in _load_data_and_files still references old attribute names 'self.POST' and 'self._post' which no longer exist after the rename
findings.failure_scenario: No runtime failure, but the outdated comment at lines 380-383 ('self.POST, set self._post and self._file to prevent attempts to parse POST data again') misleads future maintainers about the actual attributes (self.data, self._data, self._files) that _mark_post_parse_error sets.
